description: Comprehensive multi-subtree extraction benchmark reconstructed from production logs of thread 736b1b30 (LG 34GS95QE-B vs MSI MPG 341CQPX, 84 comments, 11 extraction subtrees). The fixture lifts every input the production extraction prompt saw — thread context, OP summary, cheat sheet, per-subtree resolved products with real DB specs, and the identification annotations — directly out of the logs CSV at docs/thread-extraction/736b1b30-d7da-4ddf-8504-a6957b64c789-logs.csv. The dataset exercises every realistic extraction case the prompt ever encounters in this thread: hands-on owner reports with detailed multi-attribute evidence, prospective-buyer deliberations with reasoned preferences, anti-recommendations, comparison-baseline leakage traps ("coming from a 165Hz Acer Predator IPS"), settings/spec dumps that should not produce quotes, multi-product subtrees where attribution must split correctly, and rare wrong-variant identifications (e.g. MPG431CQPX) that the prompt must preserve verbatim. Use this as the realistic counterpart to monitors-extraction-tiny — tiny is for quick offline iteration; this one is for measuring how candidate prompts and models behave on production-shaped inputs across an entire thread's worth of subtrees.

expectations.desiredOutcome: For every PLAN comment in every subtree, produce schema-valid extraction output. The most important global signals: (1) hands-on owners (e.g. AnurinXx with [used: MSI MPG341CQPX] affinity, makemesplooge, valorshine) must be classified experience='owner' or 'prior_owner' with non-empty quotes when the body contains substantive verdicts; (2) prospective buyers should still get quotes when the verdict attaches to a named attribute (price, panel finish, design, certification, refresh rate) and empty quotes when only vague verdicts like 'huge gamble' or 'best option' are present; (3) anti-recommendations (Corsair Xeneon overpriced, ASUS ROG too expensive) must surface as negative-sentiment quotes on the correct product, never bleed onto the recommended product; (4) comparison-baseline clauses ('coming from a 165Hz Acer Predator IPS', 'the 800R curve was too much when I looked at one at Best Buy') must NOT be attached to the resolved product; (5) every subtree's response must include an entry for every PLAN comment id (c0..cN), even if products is empty.

judge.instructions: Score each candidate on five dimensions, each 1-10. (1) faithfulness — quotes must be verbatim substrings of the comment body, with no fabrication. Cross-check that every quote appears in the source comment. (2) quote-gate compliance — for prospective_buyer / reference experience, quotes are only retained when attached to a named attribute (price, panel finish, panel type, refresh rate, defect, behavior under a condition). For owner / prior_owner / tested experience, a verdict alone is sufficient — no named attribute required. (3) attribution accuracy — multi-product subtrees must keep each quote on the correct product. Comparison-baseline leakage ('coming from X' clauses) must NOT attach to the resolved product. (4) completeness — every PLAN comment id (c0..cN) must receive an entry, even with empty products. Missing comment ids trigger a costly retry in production. (5) classification calibration — does experience match the speaker's relationship (owner with purchase evidence vs prospective_buyer researching), does depth reflect the substance of the evaluation, are intents appropriate (recommendation vs experience_report vs warning vs comparison vs issue_report)? Return JSON {candidates:[{candidateId, scores:{faithfulness, quoteGate, attribution, completeness, calibration}, rationale}], verdict}. Verdict format: 'best=<id>' | 'tie' | 'none-acceptable'.
